title: Microsoft Teams: manage call groups from Teams on Mobile
summary: Hold: both Teams admin center paths omit a required selection before the control. The calling policy path needs Edit, and the user call group path needs a call-answering option and Group call pickup selection. The rollout, licence requirement and existing policy coverage are supported.

claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Manage call groups on Mobile

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let users create and manage their own call group from Teams on Mobile.
claims.quote: Users can create and manage their call group directly from Teams on Mobile.

claims.claim: Users will be able to add call group members on Mobile.
claims.quote: They can add or remove members, configure how the group should ring

claims.claim: Users will be able to remove call group members on Mobile.
claims.quote: They can add or remove members

claims.claim: Users will be able to configure how their call group rings on Mobile.
claims.quote: configure how the group should ring

claims.quote: users can forward their calls to the group or ring the group at the same time as their own devices, using the call handling options in Calling settings.

claims.claim: The Mobile route is Settings > Calling > Manage call group.
claims.quote: From Settings, users can open Calling and select Manage call group to view their current call group or create a new one.

claims.claim: The feature uses the existing call group calling policy, and users with call groups turned off cannot use it on Mobile.
claims.quote: uses the existing calling policy that controls call groups. If call groups are turned off for a user in their calling policy, they won't be able to use the feature on Mobile.

claims.claim: The sources describe no new identity or permission for Mobile call group management.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile Manage call group separate admin policy disable mobile CallGroup AllowCallGroups five members ring order; read MC1552390, call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup and Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy. No new identity or permission described.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Call sharing and group call pickup share incoming calls with colleagues who can answer while the user is unavailable.
claims.quote: let users share their incoming calls with colleagues so that the colleagues can answer calls that occur while the user is unavailable.

claims.claim: Be immediately forwarded stops incoming calls from ringing the user's own devices.
claims.quote: Be immediately forwarded so that calls to the user don't ring their devices.

claims.claim: CallGroupTargets replaces current call group membership with the complete supplied membership.
claims.quote: The members of the Call Group. You need to always specify the full set of members as the parameter value. What you set here will overwrite the current call group membership.

claims.claim: A call group can have up to 25 users.
claims.quote: Each call group can have up to 25 users.

claims.claim: A user can own only one call group.
claims.quote: A user can only own one call group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says adding more than five call group members automatically switches ring order to Everyone at once.
claims.quote: If you add more than five members to a call group, the ring order automatically switches to "Everyone at once."

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not separately describe how the new Mobile ordering options present the five-member rule.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "Mobile" "call group" "five"; read call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup and Set-CsUserCallingSettings. Both state the general five-member restriction; neither describes the new Mobile ordering UI's handling of it.

claims.claim: The call group owner and members must be in Teams Only deployment mode.
claims.quote: Users, the call group owner, and members of the call group must be in Teams Only deployment mode.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The call group policy setting is reached by Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Inbound calls can be routed to call groups.
claims.quote: Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit.
claims.fix: Replace the structured and rendered path with 'Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Inbound calls can be routed to call groups' in Teams admin center, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-calling-policy. Use that complete route in the Before rollout policy-check bullet too.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCallGroups $true enables call groups and routing inbound calls to them for users governed by the policy.
claims.quote: Enables the user to configure call groups in the Microsoft Teams client and that inbound calls should be routed to call groups.

claims.claim: Teams calling policies can be assigned to users or groups.
claims.quote: Assigns a specific Teams Calling Policy to a user, a group of users, or sets the Global policy instance.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/grant-csteamscallingpolicy?view=teams-ps to sources; it explicitly confirms group assignment, whereas the cited calling-policy overview qualifies group support with 'if supported for the policy type'.

claims.claim: The call group editor is reached by Users > Manage users > user > Voice > Call answering rules > Manage call group.
claims.quote:
Be immediately forwarded and select Group call pickup from the Call forward type dropdown
4. Select Manage call group
claims.fix: Replace the structured and rendered path with 'Users > Manage users > user > Voice > Call answering rules > Ring user's devices > Also allow > Group call pickup > Manage call group' in Teams admin center, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup. The current path omits the call-answering choice and Group call pickup selection.

claims.claim: Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity <user principal name> -CallGroupOrder InOrder -CallGroupTargets <array of sip addresses> sets one user's call group membership and ordered ringing.
claims.quote: Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity user1@contoso.com -CallGroupOrder InOrder -CallGroupTargets $cgm

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate admin UI or API switch is documented for Mobile call group management.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile Manage call group Settings Calling admin control separate policy; Teams mobile call group management PowerShell mobile specific disable Set-CsTeamsMobilityPolicy. Read call sharing, calling policies and both policy cmdlet references; no separate switch found.

claims.claim: The existing admin-side editor changes the user's call group rather than enabling or disabling the Mobile screen.
claims.quote: You can use the Teams admin center to configure group call pickup for your users.

claims.claim: The Learn call group page has no Mobile-specific management steps at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile Manage call group Settings Calling admin control separate policy; read the full call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup page. It documents Teams admin center and PowerShell procedures, not the new Mobile management steps.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: When turning off call groups, administrators must clean up call group relationships in Teams admin center to avoid incorrect routing.
claims.quote: When you turn off call groups for users, you must clean up the call group relationships for users in the Teams admin center to avoid incorrect call routing.

claims.claim: Use unanswered settings and Send to voicemail under Routing for PSTN calls take precedence over call group forwarding.
claims.quote: If Use unanswered settings or Send to voicemail is used, either of these settings will have precedence over other call forwarding settings like call forwarding with simultaneous ringing to delegate, call groups, or call forwarding.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: For the Mobile management change, the sources show an existing Teams Phone entitlement and policy/licence checks and communication work rather than a newly named licence or meter.
claims.quote: Review the calling policy assigned to the users who should be able to manage call groups, and confirm that call groups are allowed.- Confirm that those users have a Teams Phone license.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The Manage call group screen is missing for users without Teams Phone or with call groups disabled in their calling policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Manage call group" "mobile" "hidden" "license"; read MC1552390 and call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup. The notice confirms eligibility and policy restrictions, but does not state whether ineligible users see a hidden or disabled control.
claims.fix: Replace 'It is missing for users without a Teams Phone licence or with call groups turned off in the calling policy.' with 'The feature requires a Teams Phone licence; users with call groups turned off in their calling policy cannot use it on Mobile.' In the At rollout bullet say 'MC1552390 says eligible users will see Manage call group under Settings > Calling on Teams on Mobile.' Remove 'other users see nothing new' from the impact rationale.
